items.headline: Mexico vs South Africa - Estadio Azteca
items.body: The 2026 FIFA World Cup opens at Mexico City Stadium with hosts Mexico facing South Africa in Group A. This marks a rematch of the 2010 World Cup opener which ended 1-1. Mexico automatically qualified as host nation and will be among six CONCACAF teams competing in the expanded 48-team format.

items.headline: 48-Team Format Expansion
items.body: The tournament has expanded from 32 to 48 teams across 12 groups of four teams each. This first-ever expansion increases opportunities for emerging nations while maintaining competitive balance through strategic seeding. 32 teams will advance to the knockout round via group winners and best third-place finishers.

items.headline: Key Debutant Nations
items.body: Curaçao qualified as the smallest nation ever to reach the World Cup, alongside Cape Verde, Jordan, and Uzbekistan making their debuts. Eight Arab nations qualified for the first time, including Iraq who completed the longest qualifying campaign at 21 matches over 28 months.

items.headline: England Group L - Croatia Opener
items.body: England faces 11th-ranked Croatia on June 17 in a repeat of the 2018 World Cup semifinal (Croatia won 2-1). Group L also includes Ghana (74th) and Panama (33rd). Thomas Tuchel selected 26 players with notable omissions of Phil Foden, Cole Palmer, and Harry Maguire.

items.headline: Defensive Depth Concerns
items.body: Tino Livramento suffered season-ending thigh injury in recent months, while Reece James and Djed Spence recently returned from hamstring and jaw injuries. John Stones was selected despite limited Manchester City minutes due to a thigh issue, but Tuchel insists the experienced centre-back is fit for tournament duty.

items.headline: Tuchel's Selection Philosophy
items.body: Manager selected the 'best team' rather than 26 most talented players, prioritizing tournament fitness and experience. Arsenal's Bukayo Saka and Harry Kane coming off strong seasons represent key attacking threats, with multiple midfield options available including Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers.

items.headline: Group Stage Playing Schedule
items.body: Each of 48 teams plays three group matches to determine advancement. Top two teams per group plus eight best third-place finishers advance to 32-team knockout round. Tiebreakers use goal differential, goals scored, head-to-head, fair play record, and drawing of lots.

items.headline: Competitive Balance Pathway System
items.body: FIFA created two pathways to semifinals to prevent top-ranked teams meeting before final. Spain (1st) and Argentina (2nd) drawn in opposite pathways, as are France (3rd) and England (4th). This ensures elite teams cannot clash until semifinals if both win their groups.

items.headline: Tournament Dates & Venues
items.body: Group stage runs June 11-24, knockout round June 28-July 19. Finals hosted across 16 cities: 11 in USA, 3 in Mexico, 2 in Canada. Final held at New York/New Jersey Stadium on July 19 with 82,500 capacity. Opening venue is Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

items.headline: European Contingent - 16 Teams
items.body: UEFA allocated largest continental slot with established powers including Spain, France, England, Germany, and Netherlands. Italy failed to qualify for third consecutive World Cup after playoff loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina on penalties, while Sweden advanced via playoff uniquely using Nations League path.

items.headline: CONMEBOL's Elite Representation
items.body: South America sends six teams: Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, and Uruguay. Argentina led qualification with Lionel Messi's continued brilliance. Brazil finished points clear of qualification despite being ranked outside automatic spots.

items.headline: All Six Confederations Represented
items.body: First World Cup where all six confederations guaranteed at least one berth. OFC granted guaranteed slot plus possible inter-confederation playoff spot. CAF sends 10 teams including Morocco, Senegal, and historic eight Arab nations. AFC sends 8 teams; CONCACAF sends 6 (including three automatic hosts).

items.headline: Historic Qualifying Achievements
items.body: Iraq completed longest World Cup qualifying campaign at 21 matches over 28 months after first failing to qualify. Haiti won CONCACAF Group C with 11 points. Austria topped UEFA Group H with 22 goals in eight matches, including 10-0 victory over San Marino.

items.headline: Qualification Form Leaders
items.body: Morocco won African Group E with eight wins in eight games and plus-20 goal differential. South Korea won Asian Group B by six points over Jordan. Scotland won UEFA Group C with only one loss in six matches, scoring six more points than Denmark.

items.headline: Tournament Favorites & Rankings
items.body: Spain ranked highest in tournament (1st globally), followed by Argentina (2nd), France (3rd), and England (4th). Italy ranked 12th was highest-ranked non-qualifier. New Zealand (85th) lowest-ranked qualifier. 26 of 48 teams also appeared in 2022 tournament.
